judged_text: The booking row persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0] via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, so the multi-host destination set survives nowhere in the DB and every flow that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from booking.destinationCalendar collapses a COLLECTIVE booking back to host 1. Deferred-creation flows rebuild their evt from booking.destinationCalendar — confirm.handler (collective bookings with requiresConfirmation) and the Stripe/PayPal handlePaymentSuccess webhooks (paid collective bookings) then call EventManager.create with only the first host's destination, so those collective bookings get a calendar event on host 1's calendar only and never on the other hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` was changed to an array and COLLECTIVE team members’ destination calendars are appended in `handleNewBooking` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, only the first destination calendar is stored: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts). Downstream/deferred flows rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (a single relation) and wrap it as a single-element array, e.g. confirm handler and payment webhooks: `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : ...` (confirm.handler.ts, ee/payments/api/webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, etc.). Since `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` to create events for each destination, these deferred flows will only ever create a calendar event for the single persisted destination (host 1), losing the additional collective hosts’ destinations.
